content_voiceover: This table from the Mayo Clinic experience, 22 patients followed over 25 years, ranks the underlying disorders found in acquired VWD. Monoclonal gammopathy of undetermined significance, MGUS, is the single most common association at 27%, followed by multiple myeloma at 15%, non-Hodgkin lymphoma and myeloproliferative disorders each around 10%. Wilms tumor accounts for 8%, notable because it's the classic pediatric association tested on boards. Drugs contribute 7%, chronic lymphocytic leukemia and hypothyroidism each 5%, and carcinoma and hairy cell leukemia round out the rare causes. The high-yield takeaway is that lymphoproliferative and plasma cell disorders, MGUS, myeloma, and lymphoma together, account for over half of all acquired VWD cases, so any older patient with new mucocutaneous bleeding and an unexplained monoclonal protein should raise suspicion for AVWS. Hypothyroidism is also worth remembering as a reversible cause you can fix by simply correcting thyroid function.
keypoints: MGUS is the #1 cause of acquired VWD (27%)
Hypothyroidism (5%) is a reversible, correctable cause
